My proposal isn't about necessary hacking things together, although I do personally encourage it if you're limited to the confines of the engine. It's to suggest that such a change would be consistent with my interpretation of Godot's design philosophy. For consistency with `LineEdit`/`TextEdit` and the naming of other `*_changed` signals, the signal should be named `text_changed`, not `changed_text`.

As far as I understand, `Label`/`RichTextLabel` does not have the signal, since the text can only be changed via code, unlike `LineEdit`/`TextEdit`. You always know when the text changes, in the sense that the text changes on your initiative. So you can encapsulate the logic you need in a method:

```gdscript
func set_text_custom(new_text: String) -> void:
    text = new_text
    # your logic here
```

You can also inherit Label/RichTextLabel and add a signal:

```gdscript
class_name MyLabel
extends Label

signal text_changed(new_text: String)

func set_text_custom(new_text: String) -> void:
    text = new_text
    text_changed.emit(new_text)
```

What the button does and says it will do:
* Take the file and convert and load it into internal formats, so you can use it, applying the settings and options you provided

What it doesn't do (and what the word "reimport" doesn't convey):

* Delay changes, save options, etc., except as part of the first

Related bug report: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/124104. Whatever output formats are added here, the 16-bit path that exists today floors instead of rounding and has no dither, and the WASAPI (float mix format) and Web drivers hand over float that has first been cut to the 16-bit grid. The bug report covers that conversion, with measurements on Linux, macOS and Web. A float or 24-bit path for the drivers that are integer today (CoreAudio, PulseAudio, ALSA, OpenSL ES) is the feature that belongs in this proposal. Note that the int32_t the drivers receive today carries only 21 bits, so a float made from it is a 21-bit float; godotengine/godot#90013 writes from the mixed float instead.
